stem:
Nitya solves this digit-in-disguise addition. Each letter stands for one digit, and different letters stand for different digits.

$$\begin{array}{c@{}c@{}c} & A & B \\ + & A & B \\ \hline & C & A \end{array}$$

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: Letter is only a name for the sum; the digit values need not fit the addition.
Each letter stands for one fixed digit from $0$ to $9$, and different letters stand for different digits.
Units and tens columns must add with carries exactly as in ordinary addition.
The largest-looking letter must be digit $9$.

teacher.key_rationale: A cryptarithm assigns one digit per letter and must satisfy place-value column addition with carries. Treating "letter" as the answer label skips the digit model. Picking 9 from how large a letter looks is surface capture.
